_notes: TEMPLATE, not a runnable config -- copy this file, don't edit it in place, when
adding a new review beyond the 3 already vetted (reviews/van_de_Schoot_2018/,
reviews/Appenzeller-Herzog_2019/, reviews/Muthu_2021/; see runbook §2, §6).
To add review '<name>':
1. mkdir reviews/<name> && cp example_config.json reviews/<name>/config.json
2. Look up '<name>' in asreview/synergy-dataset's datasets.toml (GitHub repo root)
-- its 'eligibility_criteria' field under [datasets.publication] for that key --
and reflow it into default_prompt as shown above. Verify word for word against
the live file; don't paraphrase from memory or assume an earlier summary was
complete (reviews/Appenzeller-Herzog_2019/config.json's _notes has a worked
example of a paraphrase that silently dropped two real exclusion criteria on a
first pass).
3. Write reviews/<name>/reviews.toml (see reviews/Muthu_2021/reviews.toml for the
minimal one-review shape): `reviews = ["<name>"]`.
4. Confirm the review's record/inclusion counts with `synergy_dataset show <name>`
before a real run -- don't assume numbers from memory or another review's table.
5. Run with the new subfolder, e.g.:
make all REVIEWS_FILE=reviews/<name>/reviews.toml CONFIG=reviews/<name>/config.json \
RUN_DIR=data/run_<name> TRACK=<name> \
VALIDATE_OUT=results/validation_record_<name>.json
Every field except default_prompt is identical across all per-review config files by
design -- the same fixed instrument (vendors, aggregation, tau, batch_size,
zero_policy) is what's being proven reliable across reviews, so it must not vary
between them. See reviews/van_de_Schoot_2018/config.json's _notes for the full
history/rationale behind every other field (tau derivation, model pinning,
temperature, zero_policy, the track_prompts -> default_prompt migration) -- not
duplicated here.
This file is not read literally beyond 'vendors' (including each vendor's
'temperature'), 'aggregation', 'tau', 'batch_size', 'zero_policy', 'default_prompt',
'track_prompts' (unused here), and 'confidence_threshold' (see
attest.cli._load_ensemble_config) -- this _notes field is ignored by the loader and
safe to keep as documentation. That said: this specific file is a template only --
its default_prompt is not valid input for a real `attest screen` call.
'batch_size' (attest.provenance.config.Config.batch_size, "b_e") is set to 1
explicitly here, same as in every reviews/<name>/config.json -- one record per
screening request, this pipeline's actual instrument, stated outright rather than
left to attest's own fallback default (also 1) -- see reviews/README.md's
batch_size section for the full rationale.
